caption: A pat of cold butter is dropped into a hot frying pan, and it melts into a spreading pool of liquid.

sa.check: A pat of butter is dropped into a frying pan.
The butter melts: it loses its block shape and turns to liquid.
A pool of liquid butter spreads across the pan.
The butter starts as a solid pat with square edges.
The drop comes first and the melting follows.

pc.expect: The melting runs one way: the pat softens, slumps and shrinks while the pool around it grows, and each change persists.
pc.fail: The pat regains its square edges or its height; or the pool shrinks back into the pat; or the butter firms into a solid block again in the pan; or the pat alternates between softer and firmer.

pc.expect: The melted butter flows as a thin liquid that runs to the pan's low places and wets its surface; the unmelted pat is a soft solid that slides on the film.
pc.fail: The pool stands as a dome or holds a fixed shape as the pan is tilted; or the melt moves as a solid slab across the pan; or the pat shatters into dry pieces; or the liquid stands in a heap above the pan's surface.

pc.expect: The pool spreads outward and downhill across the pan's floor and runs to its lowest side.
pc.fail: The pool climbs the pan's sloping wall and stays there; or a run of butter travels uphill; or liquid butter lifts off the pan and floats.

pc.expect: The melt starts where the butter meets the pan: the pat's underside goes glossy and the film spreads out from beneath it.
pc.fail: A pool spreads on the pan while the pat is still sharp-edged and dry underneath; or the pat melts from its top face while its underside stays solid and matt; or the pool appears on a part of the pan the butter never touched.

pc.expect: One pat of butter; matter moves only from the pat into the pool, and the pan keeps its shape.
pc.fail: The pat grows; or a second pat appears; or the pool vanishes at a stroke; or butter appears outside the pan with none crossing the rim; or the pat passes through the pan's base.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The pan's finish, the hob and the things around it stay the same.
pc.fail: The pan's finish changes pattern; or the hob's knobs move; or items around the pan rearrange.

note: Browning of the butter is chemistry and is outside the branch; a deepening golden colour is not judged.
